name: Tandoori-Style Chicken Thighs
summary: Bone-in thighs marinated in spiced yogurt and roasted hot, served with rice and a yogurt-lemon sauce.

ingredients.name: chili powder (or cayenne for more heat)

instructions: Mix 250 g of the yogurt with the garlic, ginger, the juice of half the lemon, the chili, cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, oil, and 1.5 tsp salt.
Cut 2–3 deep slashes in each thigh and coat in the marinade. Refrigerate at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Lay the thighs skin-side up on a foil-lined baking sheet and roast 35–40 minutes until charred at the edges and 175°F (80°C) inside.
While it roasts, cook the rice: 300 g rice with 600 mL water, simmered covered for 15 minutes, then rested 5 minutes.
Stir the remaining 125 g yogurt with the juice of the other lemon half and a pinch of salt. Serve the chicken over rice with the sauce.

glutenFree.notes: Chicken, plain yogurt, rice, and spices are naturally gluten-free. Check the garam masala label for added flour.

budgetNotes: The yogurt marinade tenderizes cheap bone-in thighs. Overnight is best, but one hour works.

Substitution: a hot home oven replaces a tandoor (clay oven), and the red food colouring is left out. The taste changes: a tandoor cooks at about 480°C and adds smoky char that a home oven can't match, so this is closer to a well-spiced roast chicken. Broil for the last 3–4 minutes for more char. Without the colouring the chicken comes out orange-brown, not red. That only affects looks.
If the budget allows, a cucumber ($1.50) grated into the yogurt sauce makes a proper raita. That puts the total at about $14.60.
